newsitem.title: USA: G7 stressed interest in strong dollar - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: G7 stressed interest in strong dollar - Tietmeyer.

text.p: The Group of Seven rich nations stressed their interest in a strong U.S. dollar in talks on Saturday and also said the planned European currency must be stable, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said.

Tietmeyer told a briefing after the G7 talks, held in Washington ahead of next week's annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, "All parties stressed that they were interested in a strong dollar."
The interest in the planned Euro single currency being a stable replacement for the mark was also shared by all, he added, saying this was important for calm currency markets.

"The others are interested in the fact that when the mark disappears its successor currency should be able to take exactly the role of the mark," Tietmeyer said, noting that the mark is the world's second most important reserve currency.
"Otherwise there could be flight into the dollar which would have consequences in the currency markets. No one is interested in that happening," he continued.
Europe plans to create a single currency with an as-yet unspecified number of participant countries from 1999. The new Euro is expected to be an important reserve currency.
